audit.whatIsWrong: Six separate strings call Rebuttal Mel's ultimate and say it reflects Nasus's damage back at him (whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1]).
audit.why: Rebuttal is Mel's W — cooldown 38/35/33/29/26, cost 80/60/40/20/0, range 250. It reflects PROJECTILES and prevents her from taking damage. Nasus owns no projectile anywhere in his kit: Siphoning Strike is a melee auto-attack reset, Spirit Fire is a ground-targeted zone, Wither is a targeted debuff and Fury of the Sands is a self-centred aura. Nothing of his is ever reflected back at him, so the only clause that matters to a Nasus is the damage immunity. Mel's actual ultimate is Golden Eclipse (120/100/80s, range 25000 — effectively global), which strikes every enemy marked with Overwhelm for damage scaling on stack count, and was never mentioned once.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is a W on a 38s rank-1 cooldown that blanks damage outright — bait it before you spend a stacked Q. The level-6 threat is Golden Eclipse detonating Overwhelm stacks from anywhere on the map.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown number anywhere in the matchup; breakdown.cooldowns described Solar Snare in purely vague terms.
audit.why: Rebuttal at rank 1 is a 38-second cooldown — the longest punish window in the lane and the single most actionable number a Nasus can hold. Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 on a 1000 range while Wither only reaches 700, so she outranges his one answer and he has to close the gap rather than trade at range.
audit.corrected: State the 38s Rebuttal window and the 1000-vs-700 range gap explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is HARD and diffRating 7/10 on a 58.44% win rate across 527 games.
audit.why: 58.44% is the second-highest win rate in the entire Nasus top-lane table, yet it carries the same HARD 7/10 label as Quinn at 45.30%. The level chart itself (Mel ahead levels 2-6, Nasus ahead from first item) is correct and stays as is — it is the overall label that contradicts the data.
audit.corrected: EVEN / 6/10 with the matching tone colour already used elsewhere in the file, keeping the early-game-loss framing intact.

edits.before: This is still her window, and the trap is her ultimate — Rebuttal reflects your incoming damage, so if you pop Fury of the Sands and dump everything into her while it's up, you do nothing and feed her. At 6, treat your R as a survival button, not an engage. Spirit Fire on the wave keeps you stacking and shreds her armor a touch, and a well-timed Wither onto her shuts off her kiting — but only commit when her ult is down. Otherwise keep farming; you're playing not to die, not to win lane yet.
edits.after: This is still her window, and the trap is Rebuttal — her W, not her ult. It stops her taking damage entirely, so a stacked Q dumped into it is a wasted cooldown and a free counter-poke for her. Bait it, then commit: at rank 1 it is down for 38 seconds. Spirit Fire on the wave keeps you stacking and shreds her armor a touch, and Wither shuts off her kiting once you are inside its 700 range. At 6 respect Golden Eclipse — it detonates her Overwhelm stacks on you from anywhere on the map, so do not linger low.

edits.before: Once your first item lands and your Q is stacked, the matchup flips hard — a squishy, immobile mage has no answer to a stacked Siphoning Strike plus Wither's massive slow once you're in range. Fury of the Sands makes you near-unkillable in a sustained fight, and unlike a hard scaler she has no percent-HP or true damage to punch through your bulk. Force sidelane 1v1s where she can't kite you and can't poke from safety; just respect her ult timer on the all-in and don't burn R into a live Rebuttal.
